author: reek
body: The discriminator is the first padding pixel of row 0, at scanline offset 800. Stepping rows by the stride never touches it. Stepping rows by the visible width puts the start of row 1 exactly there, because 1 * 800 = 800. So one pixel tells the two implementations apart, and the last row's origin at 7 * 928 is unreachable by a width-stepping walk at all.

author: reek
body: The final case is the instrument's calibration and it is the reason to trust the rows above it: the same fill is asked for the wrong pitch, and the discriminator has to flip. Without it every assertion here would be satisfied by a buffer nothing had written to.
